The RH·BOTS spec sheet attributes to the RHX2 a LiDAR and RGB-D camera, an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module (157 TOPS) with an 8-core Arm Cortex-A78AE CPU, 27 degrees of freedom and 2 m/s. rha3.claim: Adult-sized humanoid for stage performance and public-facing service
rha3.tagline: Shows, reception, presentations and entertainment, with multimodal interaction, shifts of up to 10 hours and coordinated fleet control.

rha3.intro: The RHA3 is an adult-sized bipedal humanoid designed for commercial shows, interactive entertainment, reception, presentations and exhibitions. With 55 kg and 12 kW of peak power, it performs dynamic stage movements, and its swappable dual battery allows it to work for extended periods. It includes UWB positioning as standard to coordinate groups of more than 100 robots.

12 kW of peak power and 150 A of maximum current, with a power-to-weight ratio of 0.218 kW/kg. Structure in magnesium alloy, titanium and flexible TPU.
Full-day battery life
Redundant dual battery of 1,152 Wh with up to 10 hours of use and hot-swapping in about 10 seconds, for continuous 24-hour operation.
Fleet coordination
Standard UWB positioning with accuracy under ±10 cm to coordinate more than 100 units without modification.
Multimodal interaction
Binocular vision, touch sensors on the shoulders, 360° voice pickup with multiple microphone arrays, and a front display.

rhg2.claim: Industrial humanoid with mobile base and telescopic torso
rhg2.tagline: Two manipulator arms on a wheeled platform, for manufacturing, logistics, assembly, material handling and inspection.

7-DOF arms with joint torque sensors and force control, with sub-millimetre precision operations announced by the manufacturer.
Autonomous mobile platform
Ackermann steering, lateral movement, in-place rotation, 360° perception and automatic charging station.
High-performance computing
NVIDIA Jetson Thor T5000 with 2,070 TFLOPS announced at FP4 precision, for perception and skill learning.

rhc5.tagline: Scrubbing, vacuuming, debris collection and dust mopping in a single pass, with autonomous navigation and remote task management.

Cleaning a spill in a hospital

Combined sweeping, scrubbing and drying, with a side brush for edges and corners. Debris removal above 95%.

Fusion of LiDAR, RGB depth vision and IMU with real-time SLAM and 2D/3D maps. It plans routes, avoids obstacles and resumes the task after an interruption.
Dual 45-litre tank
90 litres of total liquid capacity with secondary treatment of dirty water and tank self-cleaning in 4 minutes.
Building integration
Wi-Fi, 4G and LoRa, with elevator integration and access control to work across different floors and areas.

mt1.claim: Autonomous AI sweeper for large areas
mt1.tagline: Sweeps fine dust and bulky debris in a single pass and works unsupervised shift after shift, with automatic charging at its station.

Its dual-disc brushes pick up everything from fine dust to leaves and bottles, and its AI cameras locate debris for spot cleaning. The dual-disc brushes pick up leaves and bottles while sweeping fine dust and dirt at the same time.
AI debris recognition
The cameras identify different types of debris in real time; in spot-cleaning mode it covers up to 6,000 m²/h.
Active dust control
High-flow negative-pressure ventilation and a filter retain particles in the bin and prevent them from returning to the air.
Continuous operation
Up to 8 h of battery life, charging in about 3 h, and automatic docking at the station to work in shifts.

t150.claim: Autonomous industrial transport robot for 150 kg
t150.tagline: Moves material between plant and warehouse stations without construction work or a server. It is up and running within an hour and operates in continuous shifts with quick battery swapping.

Open integration
It is controlled from the screen, Pager, the PUDU Link app or API, and connects with lifts, doors, WMS, MES and ERP systems.

t600.claim: Autonomous lifting robot for 600 kg loads
t600.tagline: Lifts and moves pallets, shelving units and carts of up to 600 kg between warehouse and line. Its column with handles allows it to be moved by hand with electric assistance when needed.

t600.intro: The T600 is the lifting (Lifting) version of the T600 series: an autonomous mobile robot that positions itself under pallets, shelving units or carts, lifts them 60 mm and moves them with up to 600 kg of load. It navigates with VSLAM and LiDAR, features a 10.1-inch screen and is designed for internal logistics of heavy loads in manufacturing and warehouses.
keyfacts: 6 h at full load, 12 h unloaded
highlights: 600 kg per trip
Moves entire pallets and shelving units, reducing the number of trips and intermediate handling.
Column with handles and assistance
The column incorporates a screen and handles; manual handling has speed-controlled electric assistance.
VSLAM and LiDAR navigation
It combines ceiling-based localization with two LiDAR units and RGBD cameras, and recognizes shelving groups to pick up and set down the load at its location.

Autonomous locations and fleet
Detects which locations are occupied, chooses destination and route, and coordinates multiple units without a network or server.
360° perception
3D and 2D LiDAR, cameras, contour projector and LiDAR at the fork tips: stops for moving objects and goes around fixed obstacles.

omnihand.intro: OmniHand is a five-finger robotic hand that mounts as an end effector on humanoid robots, robotic arms and mobile manipulators. It combines 16 degrees of freedom, 10 of them active, in 180 × 85 × 38.5 mm and around 550 g. It is designed for interaction with people, service robotics, teaching and research.
highlights: Built for large-scale deployment
Compact, lightweight format, designed to integrate into common humanoid robots and mobile manipulators.
10 active joints and 6 passive joints
Covers common gestures and most grip types, enabling collaboration with people beyond simply picking up objects.
Fast response
Opens and closes in 0.5 s and repeats fingertip position with a typical accuracy of 0.3 mm.
Open integration
CAN-FD or RS485 communication, compatibility with Dex-UMI and ROS 2, Python and C++ SDK, and OTA updates.

Safe contact

Back-of-hand interaction

Robust sensors

omnihand-pro-2025.intro: OmniHand Pro 2025 is a five-finger robotic hand with 19 degrees of freedom, 12 of them active, designed to be mounted as an end effector on humanoid robots and robotic arms. It integrates tactile sensors with three-axis force sensing at the fingertips and single-axis sensing in the palm, and offers a five-finger grip force of 10 kg.
highlights: More active joints
12 active degrees of freedom out of 19; the index and middle fingers offer up to 14° of abduction, and the thumb rotates up to 42°.
Three-axis touch sensing at the fingertips
Measures force on three axes at the fingertips and on one axis in the palm, with 0.1 N resolution and a range of 0 to 50 N.
Rugged construction
The sensors withstand up to 1,000 N without damage, and the hand operates between -20 and 50 °C.
Simple integration
12 to 24 V power supply, CAN-FD communication, and OTA updates.

omnipicker.intro: OmniPicker is a two-finger robotic gripper for robotic arms and humanoid robots. It combines 140 N of grip force, 120 mm of stroke, and tactile sensing at the fingertips with 0.1 N resolution. It is used in sorting and logistics, in data capture to train embodied AI systems, and in continuous production operations.
highlights: Industrial reliability
The 140 N grip force is validated over one million cycles at full load.
Adaptive grip with touch sensing
Tactile sensors on the gripping surface, with 0.1 N resolution, for handling standard parts, irregular shapes, and delicate objects with force control.
Built for data collection
Compatible with Dex-UMI and with an optional depth or fisheye camera, for capturing manipulation data and training models.
Open integration
CAN FD or RS485 communication, ROS 2, and an SDK in Python and C++.
